pins.head: COUNT THE DECALS FIRST
pins.title: Adhesive Vinyl Roll Yield: How Many Decals a Roll Actually Gives
pins.desc: A 12 by 10 foot roll sounds like plenty until weeding margins and nesting waste take their cut. Work out how many finished decals you need, add the spacing between them, and buy the roll length from that number instead of guessing. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: Two rolls of adhesive vinyl in sage and cream on a cutting mat beside a small calculator, pencil and notepad at a sunlit workbench, with the headline Count the Decals First.

pins.head: BUY THE YEAR, NOT THE TUBE
pins.title: Toothpaste Multipack Planning: Size the Pack to the Household
pins.desc: A multipack only saves money if the drawer holds it and the tubes get used before they harden. Count how many people brush twice a day, work out the ounces a year takes, and buy the pack that lands closest without overshooting. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: An open bathroom drawer with clear divider trays holding upright white toothpaste tubes and spare brush heads, with the headline Buy the Year, Not the Tube.

pins.head: RELEASE BEATS FORCE
pins.title: Resin Mold Release and Cleanup: Get the Piece Out Without Tearing It
pins.desc: Most torn molds are demolded too early or pulled from the middle. Wait for a full cure, flex the rim inward all the way round, and let the piece drop out on its own. Follow the product instructions for any release agent you use. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: Hands flexing an amber resin disc out of a round silicone mold on a black work mat, with two finished amber coasters beside it and the headline Release Beats Force.

pins.head: MEASURE THE SHELF FIRST
pins.title: Clear Pantry Bins in a 6 Pack for a Shallow Kitchen Shelf
pins.desc: A bin that is an inch too deep leaves the door catching every time. Measure the shelf depth and the height under the shelf above before you buy, then pick a set that lines up front to back with room to pull out. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: Three storage bins in different sizes, one solid grey, one clear and one blue wire, on a kitchen counter beside a steel ruler and a cloth tape measure, with the headline Measure the Shelf First.

pins.head: THE POUCH IS THE SAVINGS
pins.title: Shampoo and Body Wash Refills: Where the Refill Actually Pays
pins.desc: The bottle is most of what you pay for the first time and none of what you need the second. Keep one good pump bottle per product, compare refills by the ounce rather than the pack, and check that the formula name matches before reordering. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: Two pump bottles and two standing refill pouches on a bright bathroom counter beside a rolled towel, with the headline The Pouch Is the Savings.

pins.head: BRISTLES UP, ALWAYS
pins.title: Brush Care and Station Reset: Five Minutes That Save the Brushes
pins.desc: Acrylic left in the ferrule is what splays a brush, not the painting. Rinse before the paint sets, dry the bristles pointing up so water cannot run into the handle, and reset the water jar and cloth while you are there. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A wooden drying rack holding paint brushes bristles upward beside a clean glass jar and a folded cloth on a wooden table, with the headline Bristles Up, Always.

pins.head: PRICE IT PER SCOOP
pins.title: Protein Powder Buying Guide: Compare by the Serving, Not the Tub
pins.desc: Tubs are sold by weight but used by the scoop, and scoop sizes are not the same between brands. Divide the price by the number of servings on the label, then check the protein per serving so the cheaper tub is not simply a smaller dose. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A large cream protein tub with its lid off and a wooden scoop resting on top, beside a clear shaker bottle and a folded towel on a kitchen counter, with the headline Price It Per Scoop.

pins.head: TWO TEMPS, ONE GUN
pins.title: A Dual-Temperature Hot Glue Gun for Foam and Fabric Alike
pins.desc: High heat melts foam and warps thin plastic; low heat will not hold on wood. A gun that switches between the two covers both without a second tool. Follow the product instructions and let it cool fully before storing. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A hot glue gun resting on its wire stand beside a bottle of white craft glue, a roll of masking tape and a craft knife on a wooden work table, with the headline Two Temps, One Gun.

pins.head: HOOKS BEFORE FURNITURE
pins.title: Small Entryway for Renters: Hooks and a Tray Before Any Furniture
pins.desc: A narrow hallway cannot take a bench, and a bench is rarely what the mess needs. Put hooks at coat height, a tray on the floor for wet shoes and one shallow shelf for keys, and the entryway clears itself without a single hole in the wall. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A narrow entryway with a floating shelf and small plant, a tote bag on a wall hook, and a tray of shoes on a runner rug by the front door, with the headline Hooks Before Furniture.
